mainTopic: Why one who violates his sister both pays and is lashed: עולא's answers, his rule that money replaces lashes, and the search for its source
overview: The גמרא is resolving a contradiction. Our משנה says a man who violates his sister pays a קנס, but the משנה in מכות says he gets מלקות, and we hold that a person is not both lashed and made to pay. עולא answers that our משנה is about a נערה, who gets a קנס, while the מכות משנה is about a בוגרת, who gets none. The גמרא pushes that even a בוגרת is owed בושת, פגם and צער, so the lashes case is narrowed to a שוטה who was מפותה. It adds that the lashes case could even be a נערה who is a יתומה and מפותה, since then no money is owed. From עולא's answer the גמרא draws his rule: wherever money and lashes both apply, one pays and is not lashed. It then searches for his source. It tries חובל בחבירו, then עדים זוממין, and rejects each because it has a special strict side and a special lenient side. Next it tries a הצד השוה from both cases, but challenges that too, because both cases share having some strict side and some lenient side. The discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A person is not both lashed and made to pay
steps.stepSummary: The final piece of the challenge: we hold that one is not both lashed and made to pay, so how can he get both for his sister?
steps.simpleTranslation: And we hold that a person is not both lashed and made to pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge. If the man is lashed for being with his sister, he should not also pay the קנס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה makes him pay a קנס for his sister. The משנה in מכות says he gets מלקות for her. Since the rule is אינו לוקה ומשלם, both cannot apply to the same act, so the two משניות seem to contradict.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold / it is established for us
One is not both lashed and made to pay for one act

phrases.english: And we hold that he is not both lashed and made to pay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contradiction raised just before this section
steps.kashyaTarget: Our משנה, which makes the man pay a קנס for his sister
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה in מכות lashes him for his sister, and one cannot be both lashed and made to pay

steps.title: עולא: one משנה is about a young girl, the other about an adult
steps.stepSummary: עולא splits the cases: our משנה is a נערה (fine, no lashes), and the מכות משנה is a בוגרת (lashes, no fine).
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: It is not difficult. Here it is his sister who is a young girl; there it is his sister who is an adult.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the contradiction by saying the two משניות are talking about two different sisters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קנס is only paid for a נערה. So for a נערה he pays and is not lashed. For a בוגרת there is no קנס, so nothing stops the lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl from age 12 for about six months
An adult woman, past the נערה stage

phrases.english: Ulla said: It is not difficult:
here it is about his sister who is a young girl,
phrases.notes: "Here" is our משנה, where he pays the fine.

phrases.english: there it is about his sister who is an adult.
phrases.notes: "There" is the משנה in מכות, where he gets lashes.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות speak about the same sister
steps.terutzMaskana: Fine for a נערה, lashes for a בוגרת

steps.title: But an adult sister still gets shame and damage payments
steps.stepSummary: Even for a בוגרת he owes בושת and פגם, so there is still money, and he should not be lashed.
steps.simpleTranslation: With his adult sister too, isn't there payment for shame and damage?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks עולא's answer. Even without a קנס, there is other money owed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Payment for בושת and פגם is owed even for a בוגרת. So the money-instead-of-lashes problem comes back.

phrases.english: His sister who is an adult also —
but there is shame and damage!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲחוֹתוֹ בּוֹגֶרֶת נָמֵי, הָא אִיכָּא בּוֹשֶׁת וּפְגָם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Money for בושת and פגם is still owed, so he should still not be lashed

steps.title: The case is a mentally incompetent woman
steps.stepSummary: The lashes case is a שוטה, for whom there is no בושת or פגם payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is about a woman who is a שוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing the case to a שוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שוטה is treated as not having this kind of shame or loss of value. So no money is owed, and he can be lashed.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who is mentally incompetent

phrases.english: With a mentally incompetent woman.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any adult sister owes בושת and פגם
steps.terutzMaskana: With a שוטה there is no בושת or פגם

steps.title: But there is still payment for pain
steps.stepSummary: Even with a שוטה, a forced act causes pain, which must be paid for.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes again: even a שוטה suffers צער, and that costs money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he forced her, he owes payment for צער. That is money again, so lashes should still be blocked.

phrases.english: But there is pain!

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Payment for צער is still owed, so there is still money

steps.title: The case is a woman who was seduced
steps.stepSummary: The case is a מפותה, who agreed, so there is no payment for pain.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is about a seduced woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that she was seduced, not forced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Payment for צער applies only when she is forced. A מפותה agreed, so no צער is owed. Now there is no money at all, and he is lashed.
steps.whatToRemember: The lashes case in מכות is a בוגרת who is a שוטה and was מפותה, so there is no money owed at all.

phrases.english: With a seduced woman.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: A שוטה still gets צער payment
steps.terutzMaskana: A מפותה gets no צער payment

steps.title: Now even a young sister can work: an orphan who was seduced
steps.stepSummary: Since we are already using מפותה, the lashes case can even be a נערה who is a יתומה and was seduced.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have come to this, you can even say it is his young sister, when she is an orphan and was seduced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another way to read the lashes case, building on the idea of מפותה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קנס of a מפותה normally goes to her father. If he has died, it goes to her, and since she agreed, nothing is owed. So even a נערה can be a case of lashes with no money.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have come to this

phrases.english: Now that you have come to this,
phrases.notes: "This" means the answer of a seduced woman.

phrases.english: you can even say it is his sister who is a young girl,
when she is an orphan and seduced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the מפותה idea from step 6 to offer a different setting than עולא's בוגרת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lashes case had to be a בוגרת
steps.terutzMaskana: It can even be a נערה who is a יתומה and מפותה

steps.title: עולא's rule: pay the money, skip the lashes
steps.stepSummary: From עולא's answers we see his rule: wherever there is both money and lashes, one pays and is not lashed.
steps.simpleTranslation: So עולא holds: wherever there is money and lashes, he pays the money and is not lashed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a general rule out of עולא's answers. This sets up the next question about where he gets it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא kept the נערה case as money only, with no lashes. That shows he holds that money wins over lashes, not the other way around.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think he gets lashes and is free from paying. עולא says the opposite: he pays, and the lashes fall away.

phrases.english: Apparently Ulla holds:
anywhere that there is money and lashes,
he pays the money, he is not lashed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule from עולא's answer
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When both money and lashes apply, one pays and is not lashed

steps.title: Where does עולא get this rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for עולא's source.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where does עולא know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what source teaches עולא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rule that money replaces lashes needs a basis. The גמרא wants to see where it comes from.

phrases.english: From where does Ulla get this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule in step 8
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for money replacing lashes

steps.title: He learns it from one who injures another
steps.stepSummary: עולא learns from חובל בחבירו: there too money and lashes both apply, and he only pays.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from one who injures his fellow. Just as one who injures his fellow, where there is money and lashes, pays and is not lashed, so too anywhere there is money and lashes, he pays and is not lashed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that עולא compares all such cases to someone who injures another person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hitting someone breaks a לאו, which would bring lashes, and also causes damage that must be paid. There the law is that he only pays. עולא takes that pattern and applies it to every case of money and lashes.
steps.whatToRemember: עולא's rule: when money and lashes both apply, one pays and is not lashed. חובל בחבירו is the first source the גמרא offers for it, and the next step challenges that source.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why our משנה can make the man pay a קנס for his young sister without lashes.

phrases.english: He learns it from one who injures his fellow:
just as one who injures his fellow,
where there is money and lashes,
phrases.notes: The lashes are for hitting a person, which the תורה forbids. See דברים 25:3.

phrases.english: he pays the money, he is not lashed;
so too anywhere
that there is money and lashes,
he pays the money, he is not lashed.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A comparison to חובל בחבירו, where one pays and is not lashed

steps.title: Challenge: the injurer case is too special to learn from
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects learning from חובל בחבירו. It is unusually strict, since he pays five kinds of payment. And if money is the lighter punishment, it has a lenient side, since a court is allowed to wound someone with lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why compare to someone who injures another? That case is special, because he must pay five types of payment. And if you say money is the lighter punishment, that case is special in a lenient way too, because wounding is sometimes allowed, in court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the source just given for עולא's rule. It says חובל בחבירו is a special case, so we cannot build a general rule from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge covers both ways of seeing money. If money is the harsher punishment, the injurer gets it because his case is extra strict (five payments). If money is the lighter punishment, he gets it because his sin has a lenient side: a court itself wounds people when it gives lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: What about...? The standard opening for pointing out that a source case is special and cannot teach other cases
The five payments an injurer owes
It was allowed as an exception to its general rule

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not deciding whether money or lashes is the harsher punishment. It shows that either way, the injurer case has a special feature that could explain why money wins there.

phrases.english: What about one who injures his fellow?
For he is liable for five things.
phrases.notes: The five are damage, pain, medical costs, lost work time, and embarrassment.

phrases.english: And if money is the lenient option —
For it was permitted, as an exception to its rule, in court.
phrases.notes: When the court gives lashes, it is injuring someone, and that is allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source offered in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: Learning עולא's rule from חובל בחבירו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source case has a unique strict feature (five payments) and a unique lenient feature (allowed in court), so its outcome may not carry over to ordinary cases.

steps.title: New source: learning from false witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא instead says עולא learns from עדים זוממין. They too are liable for both money and lashes, yet they only pay, so the same holds wherever money and lashes meet.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he learns it from plotting false witnesses. With false witnesses there is both money and lashes, and they pay money but are not lashed. So too, anywhere there is both money and lashes, one pays money and is not lashed.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the injurer source failed, the גמרא offers a different source for עולא: עדים זוממין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עדים זוממין who falsely testified that someone owes money deserve both to pay and to be lashed, yet they only pay. The גמרא wants to turn this into a general rule for every case with both money and lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: Plotting false witnesses who are proven to have lied
So too, every... (turning a source into a general rule)

phrases.english: Rather, he learns from plotting witnesses:
Just as plotting witnesses,
where there is money and lashes —
he pays money,
he is not lashed;

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא מָמוֹן וּמַלְקוֹת —
phrases.english: so too anywhere there is money and lashes —
he pays money, he is not lashed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the source that Step 11 knocked down.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for עולא's rule (from Step 9)
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עדים זוממין, who are liable for money and lashes, only pay.

steps.title: Challenge: false witnesses are also too special
steps.stepSummary: עדים זוממין are unusually strict, since they are punished without a warning. And if money is the lighter punishment, they have a lenient side, since they only spoke and did no act.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why compare to plotting witnesses? They are special, because they do not need a warning before being punished. And if money is the lighter punishment, they are special in a lenient way too, because they did not do any action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the new source the same way it knocked down the first one. עדים זוממין also have special features.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Strict side: normally no one is punished by a court unless he was warned first, but עדים זוממין are punished without warning. Lenient side: they never did a physical act, they only talked. Either feature could explain why they only pay.

keyTerms.meaning: A warning given before a sin, normally needed before a court can punish
They did not do a physical action

phrases.english: What about plotting witnesses?
For they do not need a warning.
And if money is the lenient option —
For they did not do an action!
phrases.notes: All they did was testify. Speaking is not counted as a physical act.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source offered in Step 12, using the same two-sided pattern as Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: Learning עולא's rule from עדים זוממין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No warning needed (a strict feature) and no physical act (a lenient feature). Either one could be why money wins there.

steps.title: Learning from what both cases share
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now learns from both cases together. What חובל בחבירו and עדים זוממין have in common is money and lashes with payment only, so the same applies everywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he learns it from both of them. What both cases have in common is that there is money and lashes, and one pays money and is not lashed. So too, anywhere there is money and lashes, one pays money and is not lashed.
steps.whatsHappening: Since each source alone has its own special feature, the גמרא combines them and learns only from what they share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a הצד השוה argument. Each case's special feature is different, so neither feature can explain the shared result. What remains in common is simply money plus lashes leading to payment only.

keyTerms.meaning: The common side, meaning learning from what two sources share

steps.whatToRemember: When each source alone has a special feature, the גמרא can learn from what both share (הצד השוה). That only works if the shared result is not explained by some feature both cases have in common.

phrases.english: Rather, he learns from both of them:
Just as the common side between them,
that there is money and lashes —
he pays money, he is not lashed;

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא מָמוֹן וּמַלְקוֹת —
phrases.english: so too anywhere there is money and lashes —
he pays money, he is not lashed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the two sources that were each rejected alone in Steps 11 and 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A הצד השוה drawn from חובל בחבירו and עדים זוממין together.

steps.title: Challenge: both cases share a strict side and a lenient side
steps.stepSummary: The combined argument is also challenged. Both cases have some strict feature and some lenient feature, which ordinary cases lack, so the shared result may come from that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why compare to what they have in common? Both of them have a strict side. And if money is the lighter punishment, both of them have a lenient side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the הצד השוה argument. It says the two cases do share something special after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strict features are different (five payments, no warning needed), but both cases have some strict side. The lenient features are also different (allowed in court, no physical act), but both have some lenient side. Ordinary cases have neither, so the combined source still might not apply to them.

keyTerms.meaning: They have in them (both cases share)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not claim the two cases have the same strict feature. It says each has some strict feature and each has some lenient feature, and that shared fact is enough to block the הצד השוה.

phrases.english: What about the common side between them?
For they have a strict side,
phrases.notes: Five payments for the injurer, no warning needed for the witnesses.

phrases.english: And if money is the lenient option —
For they have a lenient side.
phrases.notes: Wounding is allowed in court, and the witnesses did no action.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the combined derivation in Step 14 by reusing the features raised in Steps 11 and 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The הצד השוה derivation from חובל בחבירו and עדים זוממין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both sources share having some strict side and some lenient side, which ordinary cases lack, so the shared result may depend on that.
